subject.title: [Bug]: Task and Memory Recall Is Often Too Weak to Trust Across Real Conversations

question: Should OpenClaw make project/task/session recall a default core memory contract, and which existing opt-in surfaces should become part of that default path?
rationale: Current code has multiple useful primitives, but enabling stronger recall by default affects transcript indexing, privacy boundaries, provider costs, session visibility, and plugin/core ownership.

options.title: Scope a privacy-safe default
options.body: Graduate a narrow default path, likely session memory plus Active Memory for safe chat scopes, with docs, migration/doctor checks, and live QA.

options.title: Keep recall opt-in
options.body: Leave session transcript recall and Active Memory off by default, but document the supported reliability pack and keep this issue as a tracking bug for explicit-memory failures only.

options.title: Route to plugin/package
options.body: Treat project/task memory as a specialized plugin or bundle contract unless core extension gaps are identified.

recommendation.title: Scope a privacy-safe default
recommendation.body: Graduate a narrow default path, likely session memory plus Active Memory for safe chat scopes, with docs, migration/doctor checks, and live QA.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc has recent memory docs/release history and is a good routing candidate for deciding how the default memory contract should be documented and shipped.
